wideZoneComparative.item: WIDEZONE-18, COMPARES: effectiveValue(space.regions[lateral IN {wide-left, wide-right}]) > effectiveValue(space.regions[lateral = central]). SUPPORTING, WHOLE_GAME, STRUCTURAL. Both operands derive by the register's effectiveValue rule from V2 (base 1, line L161) and V9 (magnitude of each V7 modifier whose V8b referents contain the region).
wideZoneComparative.basis: ASSUMED. The relation is authored ('earn an advantage', 'more valuable', visibility_effect 'increase'); the right operand is not. 'Central' appears nowhere in Wide Zone's knowledge. The assumption: the comparison class of 'an advantage' is the remaining playable non-channel space, which in this game is central-corridor.
wideZoneComparative.evidence: soccer-module.rc1-v3.json:6713 setup_guidance 'Actions starting in or moving through the wide channel earn an advantage (bonus point, free restart, or scoring multiplier)'; :6720 '...wide areas should become more available and more valuable'. Mirror is environmental-manipulations.ts:31-55, verbatim; constraints.ts holds only the pool-order id, not the object.
wideZoneComparative.note: The only verbatim spatial value ordering in the product is the opposite one, and it is ENGINE_ONLY: slot-mechanics-variations.ts:183 and coach-voice.ts:209. AM-16 also gives the unplaced WIDEZONE-09 a home as width(central residual) > 0, which is his third example.

centralComparative.item: CW-H-10, COMPARES, HYPOTHETICAL: effectiveValue(space.regions[lateral = central]) > effectiveValue(space.regions[lateral IN {wide-left, wide-right}]). REQUIRED, WHOLE_GAME, STRUCTURAL. Same two operands as WIDEZONE-18, operator reversed; nothing else in the hypothetical contract changed.
centralComparative.basis: AUTHORED (HYPOTHETICAL) - invented for this test only, from the test's own sentence 'Scoring in the central corridor is worth double.' No workbook holds it; do not cite, merge or promote. Its real-world twin is engine text that SD-21 keeps inert.
centralComparative.note: Written as a relationship, not as an exclusion of wide value, per his instruction. Its other items (CW-H-01/05/06) are restated with AM-17's condition.referents selector, so they address a central modifier the restated game does not hold and no longer land on mod-wide.

lines.why: AM-17 lets WIDEZONE-02.a (EXISTS) and -03 (COUNT 2) be restated with lateral IN {wide-left, wide-right} at WHOLE_GAME, escaping the own-involvement unit AM-13 empties. Two elements match a minimum of two, so neither is surplus and 4.3(2) entails each. Support comes from the existence item, not from the selector.
Identical to L21; the two channels are symmetric and the adopted rules judge them alike. This is the AM-13/AM-17 interaction the spec flagged in section 10 working as he intended.

Neither comparative touches it: 4.4 says COMPARES never entails existence and 4.5/AM-13 say selection never creates. The right operand identifies the corridor and leaves it unsupported. It returns to ENTAILED only if the hypothetical restates its own S2 EXISTS with lateral at whole-game scope - an existence item, not a selection.

The first test's silent rescue is closed. AM-17 adds condition.referents to V7, so CW-H-01 is restated 'referents contains lateral=central' and matches zero elements; it no longer entails mod-wide. Wide Zone's own V7 NOT_AUTHORED declaration reaches, so the line returns to its as-authored declared gap.

The type was carried only by 4.2's attribute carry from CW-H-01, which no longer reaches mod-wide. No V8a item remains, and Wide Zone, Neutral Player and Variable Target are all UNDECLARED for type=region.

The first test's collision was an artifact of the word 'sole' and the union trick defeated it. With AM-17, CW-H-05 selects a central-referent modifier the game does not hold and never reaches this line; WIDEZONE-11.a alone entails the referent. Correct outcome: he did not want the comparative carried as a referent-level exclusion.
Identical to L185. The whole referent-level collision path goes quiet, and the contradiction moves to where it belongs: two comparative claims over the same pair of represented properties.

Second silent rescue closed: CW-H-06 restated with the referent selector matches no element, so a central x2 no longer becomes the wide modifier's magnitude. The game leaves V9 unstated, and this is the line both comparatives depend on - it is why each is reported not evaluable rather than satisfied or violated.

lines.line: L161 - primary event base value, V2 = 1
lines.why: A region no modifier names takes the base value, so L161 carries the central operand. The central side of both comparatives therefore resolves to a value whose own support is engine-only (RPC-001-20, 'One point per qualifying event').

lines.verdictBefore: did not exist; the comparative was unplaced
lines.why: Before AM-16 the comparative was inexpressible, which was the first test's real finding. It is now placed and checked. Its left operand needs V9 (L187), which the game leaves unstated, so 4.4 reports it not evaluable. Never quietly satisfied - but never named as contradicting CW-H-10.

lines.verdictBefore: did not exist; the comparative was unplaced
lines.why: Same two operands, same unresolved left side. Two forward results that cannot both hold under any single V9, reported independently. Section 1 gives a line per (element, row); no row holds a relationship, and 4.2/4.4 do not say which line a COMPARES reaches, so section 6 never runs on the pair.

runs.whereExactly: Gate B forward. Spec rev 5 line 507 checks every NARROWS bound at its scope, and 4.4 reports an unresolved operand as 'not evaluable', never quietly satisfied - so both items appear and Gate B does not pass. It is NOT an UNRESOLVED line: no row holds a relationship and no rule says which line a COMPARES reaches. Gate A fails only on pre-existing NOT_AUTHORED lines.
runs.canItStillHideSilently: No, not on value. Make central an additional referent of mod-wide and the effectiveValue rule gives eff(central) = eff(wide): both comparatives demand a strict inequality between equal quantities, so both are VIOLATED and named. With V9 still unstated both read not evaluable. Either way the first test's all-green outcome is closed. The referent-set widening itself stays unreported.
runs.boundaryRespected: Yes. Both operands are a region's effective value, from V2 (L161) and V9 (L187) of the V7 modifier whose V8b referents contain it - rows the game holds and can evaluate. Regions are S2 elements matched by lateral against S6 (0-6 and 24-30 touchline-adjacent; 6-24 holds the 15 m midline). No pressure, opportunity, availability, difficulty or uncertainty appears as an operand.
runs.am17CreatesNothing: Correct - it creates nothing. Every region the lateral selector reaches already exists: channel-north (L21), channel-south (L27), central-corridor (L33). L33 stays INVENTED although the right operand selects it. Where existence moves (L21/L27), it moves because Wide Zone's own EXISTS/COUNT items reach whole-game scope; 4.3's necessity rule does the work, not the selector.
runs.residualConcerns: Five. (1) No rule normalises operand order, so 'a>b' and 'b<a' never meet. (2) No rule says which line a COMPARES reaches; 4.3's precedent is forward-only, so reconciliation still cannot name the pair. (3) ASSUMED may not be 'support-capable' under section 6. (4) The effectiveValue derivation is the spec's own reading, unratified. (5) The right operand rests on INVENTED L33 and engine-only L161.

wideZoneComparative.item: WZ-C1: COMPARES {row V9, selector condition.referents contains region[lateral=wide]} > {rightRow V2, rightSelector *} - the wide modifier's magnitude exceeds the base event value. This is the only value comparative Wide Zone's text supports; 'value(wide) > value(central)' has no authored sentence and I will not write it AUTHORED.
wideZoneComparative.basis: ASSUMED, not AUTHORED. setup_guidance says only 'earn an advantage'; the nearest comparative is logic_usage_note 'more available and more valuable', which names no comparand. Spec s3 makes ASSUMED a bound that never entails.
wideZoneComparative.evidence: back/src/system/sport-module/soccer-module.rc1-v3.json, tl-v0-constraint-wide-zone-advantage: 'Actions starting in or moving through the wide channel earn an advantage (bonus point, free restart, or scoring multiplier).' Nothing in the object mentions central space or compares anything to it.
wideZoneComparative.note: WIDEZONE-09's real comparative is spatial - combined channel widths under E3, AM-16's width(A)>width(B) - and it contradicts no value claim. Calling the value comparative AUTHORED would repeat the first test's 'sole referent' fiction: the collision manufactured, not found.

centralComparative.item: CW-C1 (HYPOTHETICAL): COMPARES {row V9, selector condition.referents contains region[lateral=central]} > {rightRow V9, rightSelector condition.referents contains region[lateral=wide]}.
centralComparative.basis: HYPOTHETICAL AUTHORED, mirroring CW-H-05. The real product text (slot-mechanics-variations.ts:183; coach-voice.ts:209 'Points are worth most through the middle, then wide, then deep') is ENGINE_ONLY and inert under SD-21, so as authored it still collides with nothing.
centralComparative.note: Its left operand matches zero elements: the game holds one modifier, mod-wide, whose referents are the two channels. A central-referent selector reaches no V9 line, so CW-C1 lands on no line WZ-C1 touches. Different selectors, different elements - the first test's failure mode repeated.

lines.why: WZ-C1 narrows, never entails (s4.4). The game states V9 as 'UNSTATED (a multiplier; size unstated)', so the left operand does not resolve and the item is reported not evaluable. CW-C1's central selector matches no element, so only one bound reaches this line. One bound never collides; s2's UNRESOLVED needs two on one line.

No comparative reaches V8b. COMPARES never entails a referent and never entails existence, and neither comparative names V8b as an operand row. The membership disagreement the first test found is untouched by AM-16.
AM-16 and AM-17 are both explicitly non-creating. Nothing new entails a modifier, so every comparative on V9 is evaluated over an element the audit says nothing authors.

AM-17 lets a contract select the corridor; AM-13 stops it creating one. An EXISTS with lateral=central would not rescue it either: four elements match (L10/L15/L20/L37) against a minimum of one, so s4.3(2) entails none. Any central comparative's operand names an invented element.

s4.4 evaluates against values the game holds, not values with support. The game holds V2=1, but both derivers gave L161 NOT_AUTHORED (its only evidence, RPC-001-20, is ENGINE_ONLY). So any 'satisfied' comparative here is computed from an unsupported number.

lines.line: L10, L15, L20 - area and both own halves, S6 = 0-30 m
lines.why: relativeTerms defines central as 'contains the axis midline across the width'. The midline is 15 m; area 0-30, own-half-A 0-30 and own-half-B 0-30 all contain it, as does central-corridor 6-24. Nothing makes full-width exclude central, so lateral=central is a four-way match here.

lines.line: lateral=wide - no interval test in the register
lines.verdictNow: matches nothing, or over-matches five elements
lines.why: relativeTerms holds only 'central' and 'touchline-adjacent'. AM-17 registers five lateral values; four have no interval test. Under AM-12 an unregistered term matches nothing and is a restatement defect. Map wide to touchline-adjacent and it also catches area and both halves, which touch both touchlines: five elements, three wrong.

lines.line: Gate A overlapping-modifier rule (spec rev 5 line 438)
lines.why: The rule needs two modifier elements whose conditions can hold at once. Comparatives create no element, so the game still holds one, mod-wide. AM-17's condition.referents selector lets a contract address a modifier; it does not make the game hold a second one.

runs.whereExactly: Gate B forward only. A REQUIRED comparative that is not evaluable is not 'satisfied by a property with derived support' (spec rev 5 line 507), so it fails - twice, in two unrelated contract entries. It never reaches UNRESOLVED: s2 needs two items on one line, and the two comparatives' left selectors pick different elements. Gate A fails on the 246 pre-existing NOT_AUTHORED lines, as before.
runs.canItStillHideSilently: Not silently - s4.4 forbids quiet satisfaction. But quieter: 'not evaluable' is absent from s7's result table and no gate treatment is defined, so it can be visible and non-blocking. And once a magnitude exists, two contradictory comparatives cannot both fail: the game has one state, so one is satisfied and one violated. A defect against one contract, never a named conflict between two.
runs.boundaryRespected: On operands, yes if both sides sit on V9/V2 - properties the game holds. Two risks. s4.4's effective value imputes base value 1 to central-corridor, whose functions are UNSTATED and which no value row touches: that asserts a property the resolved game does not contain. And s4.2 still permits EXCLUSION strictness on a COMPARES, which the grammar sheet forbids - check the item.
runs.am17CreatesNothing: Creates nothing: confirmed. COMPARES never entails existence, s4.5 says selection identifies, and AM-05 stops a lateral EXISTS entailing any of four matching elements. But AM-17 is under-specified: the register lists five lateral values and relativeTerms defines an interval test for one. It also collides in name with AM-22's 'lateral' (orientation), which L36's note already uses.
runs.residualConcerns: AM-16's form makes both operands register rows, but value(region) is no row - Christian's first example is unwritable as adopted. s6 needs two 'support-capable' items and s3 never says a NARROWS-only item qualifies; read strictly, no COMPARES yields UNRESOLVED. Making the two meet needs three unstated steps: bound both operand lines, reduce one side to a constant, lean on an unsupported V2.

wideZoneComparative.item: WIDEZONE-18, COMPARES: effectiveValue(regions[lateral=wide]) > effectiveValue(regions[lateral=central]). SUPPORTING, WHOLE_GAME. Under the register's own effectiveValue rule this reduces to one bound on one line the game holds: V9 at L187 must exceed 1. The reviewer's V9>V2 form is not a rival claim; it is this claim after that reduction.
wideZoneComparative.basis: ASSUMED, as both agents said. 'Earn an advantage' and 'more available and more valuable' name no comparand, and 'central' appears nowhere in Wide Zone's knowledge. Under s3 an ASSUMED item is 'a bound only; never entails', so whether it is 'support-capable' for s6 is doubtful - which alone would stop any COMPARES reaching UNRESOLVED.
wideZoneComparative.evidence: soccer-module.rc1-v3.json:6713 setup_guidance 'Actions starting in or moving through the wide channel earn an advantage (bonus point, free restart, or scoring multiplier)'; :6720 'wide areas should become more available and more valuable'. :6713 also: 'Channels are reference markers - players can choose to use them or not.'
wideZoneComparative.note: WIDEZONE-09 does get a home under 4.4's aggregate clause, but in the reviewer's form, not the deriver's: the contract ledger says it needs 'the two channels' combined S6 widths to stay under E3'. That is his width(A)>width(B) example. It is ASSUMED in the original too, and it contradicts no value claim.

centralComparative.item: CW-H-10, HYPOTHETICAL: effectiveValue(regions[lateral=central]) > effectiveValue(regions[lateral=wide]). REQUIRED, WHOLE_GAME. I take the deriver's form over the reviewer's CW-C1, because CW-C1's left operand is a central modifier the game does not hold, so it reduces to nothing and cannot contradict anything.
centralComparative.basis: AUTHORED (HYPOTHETICAL) - invented for this test only, from 'Scoring in the central corridor is worth double.' Do not cite, merge or promote. Its real-world twin (slot-mechanics-variations.ts:183; coach-voice.ts:209 'worth most through the middle, then wide, then deep') is ENGINE_ONLY and SD-21 keeps it inert.
centralComparative.note: Written as a relationship, not an exclusion, per his instruction. It reduces to V9 < 1 on the very line L187 that WIDEZONE-18 reduces to V9 > 1. That is a genuine contradiction over one quantity the game holds - the first test never got this far.

lines.verdictNow: INVENTED - the AM-17 rescue is not derivable
lines.why: Reviewer wins. The deriver's 'lateral IN {wide-left, wide-right}' has no interval test: S2 says lateral is matched by the register's relative terms, and relativeTerms holds only 'central' and 'touchline-adjacent'. AM-12 bars semantic interpretation, so it normalises to nothing. Fall back to touchline-adjacent and five elements match a minimum of two, so 4.3(2) entails none.

lines.verdictNow: INVENTED - the AM-17 rescue is not derivable
lines.why: Identical to L21, and corroborated by the contract ledger's own SCHEMA note: 'touchline-adjacent does not name which touchline and S2 has no side attribute... Needs a side selector attribute or per-touchline relative terms.' AM-17 named the values; nobody authored the tests. So spec s10's promise that AM-17 rescues these lines does not yet hold.

Outcome agreed; the deriver's 'before' is wrong. CW-H-02 is OWN_INVOLVEMENT, and AM-13 empties the hypothetical's scope exactly as it empties Wide Zone's, so it never entailed L33. The reviewer also wins the counterfactual: an EXISTS at lateral=central would not rescue it, because four elements match a minimum of one and 4.3(2) entails none.

Reviewer's 'before' is right; stage-f records 'A and B agree' on this line, so the deriver's 'silent rescue closed' overstates a delta that was not there. AM-17 does work here, for a good reason: mod-wide's referents are 0-6 m and 24-30 m, neither contains the 15 m midline, so a restated 'referents contains lateral=central' matches zero modifiers.

Deriver's line; the reviewer does not cover it. 4.2's attribute carry is explicit - an item entailing an element entails each attribute its selector fixes with '=' - and CW-H-01's condition.type=region fixed it. Restated with the referent selector, CW-H-01 reaches no modifier, so no V8a item remains on the line.

Reviewer wins the 'before' outright: stage-f's consolidated entry reads 'Reviewer upheld; no UNRESOLVED'. The first test's V8b collision was an artifact of the word 'sole' and had already been struck out, so the deriver reports closing a collision that did not exist. The now-state is agreed, and it is what he asked for: no referent-level exclusion.

Each 'before' is right on its own baseline; a rerun's baseline is the as-if-authored run, so the deriver's is the apt one. Now: the game states V9 'UNSTATED (a multiplier; size unstated)'. Both comparatives reduce to this one line - V9>1 and V9<1 - so the contradiction is real and single-line. Neither side is checkable, so both read not evaluable.

lines.line: L161 - primary event base value, V2 = 1
lines.why: Both agree. A region no modifier names takes the base value, so L161 carries the whole central operand. The central side of both comparatives is computed from a number whose only evidence is RPC-001-20, which SD-21 makes inert. 4.4 evaluates against what the game holds, not what has support, so the comparison runs on an unsupported number.

lines.line: L10, L15, L20 - area and both halves, S6 0-30 m
lines.why: Reviewer's find, verified. The register's 'central' test is 'contains the axis midline across the width'; E3 is 30, so the midline is 15, and area 0-30, own-half-A 0-30 and own-half-B 0-30 all contain it, as does central-corridor 6-24. Nothing makes full-width exclude central, so any central EXISTS entails none of the four under 4.3(2).

lines.line: lateral - four of five values have no interval test
lines.why: Reviewer's find, verified in two documents. The grammar sheet and S2 both list wide-left, wide-right, wide, central, full-width; relativeTerms defines only 'central' and 'touchline-adjacent'. The one usable test over-matches, and 'lateral' collides in name with AM-22's 'lateral' (which way an element runs), already in use on L36.

lines.verdictBefore: did not exist; the comparative was unplaced
lines.verdictNow: not evaluable; Gate B forward does not pass
lines.why: This is the real gain, and it is his. Before AM-16 the claim was inexpressible, which was the first test's finding; it is now written and checked. Its left operand needs V9 (L187), which the game leaves unstated, so 4.4 reports it not evaluable and never quietly satisfied. But it is never named as contradicting CW-H-10.

lines.verdictBefore: did not exist; the comparative was unplaced
lines.verdictNow: not evaluable; Gate B forward does not pass
lines.why: Same single unresolved operand, opposite direction. Two forward results that cannot both hold under any one V9, reported independently in two unrelated contract entries. Section 1 gives a line per (element, row); no row holds a relationship, and neither 4.2 nor 4.4 says which line a COMPARES reaches, so section 6 never runs on the pair.

lines.line: The all-green configuration - central as an extra referent
lines.verdictBefore: every line entailed; the constraint silently dead
lines.verdictNow: both comparatives violated and named, once V9 resolves
lines.why: Deriver's point, and the most valuable single gain from AM-16. Name central an additional referent and the effectiveValue rule gives eff(central) = eff(wide); both claims demand a strict inequality between equal quantities, so both are violated and reported. The first test's all-green outcome is closed. With V9 unstated both read not evaluable instead.

judged.whereExactly: Gate B forward, spec rev 5 line 507. CW-H-10 is REQUIRED and is not 'satisfied by a property with derived support'; WIDEZONE-18 is a NARROWS bound not shown to 'hold at its scope'. Two clauses, two failures. It is NOT UNRESOLVED (s6): no rule maps a COMPARES onto a line, and s3 makes an ASSUMED item a bound only. Gate A fails separately on 246 pre-existing NOT_AUTHORED lines.
judged.canItStillHideSilently: Not on the value claim - 4.4 forbids quiet satisfaction and both items surface. Three quieter paths remain: the pair is never named as opposed, two rows among hundreds; 'not evaluable' has no row in s7's table, no gate treatment, so it can be visible yet non-blocking; once a magnitude exists, one comparative is satisfied and one violated - a defect against one contract, not a named conflict.
judged.boundaryRespected: Yes. Both operands reduce to V2 (L161) and V9 (L187), rows the game holds. No pressure, opportunity, availability, difficulty or uncertainty appears. eff(central)=base rests on a closed-world read of V8b, which s8 permits: mod-wide's referent list is stated and V7 holds one modifier. Defect: s4.2 and the register let a COMPARES exclude under EXCLUSION strictness; the grammar sheet forbids it.
judged.am17CreatesNothing: Correct, and AM-13 held. Every region a lateral selector reaches already exists; L33 stays INVENTED although the right operand selects it; the V7 referent selector identifies mod-wide without creating it. But AM-17 supports less than spec s10 promised: it does not rescue L21/L27, because four of its five values have no interval test and the fifth over-matches.
judged.residualConcerns: Four for him. (1) Which line a COMPARES reaches - the only thing blocking UNRESOLVED. (2) Ratify or reject the effectiveValue rule; without it his value(A)>value(B) example is unwritable. (3) Interval tests for wide-left/wide-right/wide/full-width; 'lateral' also collides with AM-22. (4) Is an ASSUMED item support-capable for s6? Minor: 'not evaluable' has no row in s7.
